ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 no-show cancellation fee; close the rider's dispute. No account action against the driver on this trip.
ruling.reasoning: NS-0 routes this case by cancelled_by = driver claiming a rider no-show, so NS-1/NS-2 govern [F4][NS-0]. NS-1's three elements are all settled by system records: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 17:19:15 (a driver_tap, not a platform auto-confirm) [F6]; at that moment he was 41 m from the pickup, inside the 200 m arrival radius [F6][F1]; and he then stayed inside 200 m for 220 s continuously until he cancelled at 17:22:55 [F6][F4]. 220 s > 180 s, so element (iii) is met and the $6.61 fee stands [F6][F4][F7][NS-1]. The rider advocate's contrary reading fails on the clause's own wording: NS-1 (iii) counts waiting only from the tap ("按下之后…连续等待"), so the earlier 5 min 5 s of presence inside 200 m is not added to the post-tap period but neither does it shorten it — the post-tap period independently exceeds the threshold [F2][F5][F6][NS-1]. The driver's chat #2 at 17:22 announcing "3 min up" is a statement, not a clock; it does not subtract from the measured 220 s [F10][F6][NS-1]. The driver's written statement claiming he waited over 3 minutes (F12) adds nothing to the system records and is not relied on [F12][NS-1]. There is no GPS hole in the wait window, so no referral under G12 is needed [F2][F3][F4][NS-1]. Because NS-1's conditions are satisfied, NS-2 (full refund) is not engaged, and the fee is correctly charged under NS-0 [F7][NS-2][NS-0]. NS-2's flag_account limb is not triggered: that consequence attaches where the driver tapped "I'm Here" while outside the pickup radius, and here the tap was 41 m from the pickup [F6][NS-2]. RD-6 likewise does not bite because no deviation or refundable overcharge is established; the driver's prior upheld no-show disputes (F17) are profile facts that cannot decide this case and support no add-on action on this trip [F17][RD-6]. The rider's version — that they came out a minute after cancellation (complaint) — is unsupported by any chat fact (the record contains only the driver's two messages) and the record does not show the rider entering the radius, so the fee is not disturbed on that account [F11][F9][F10][NS-1]. Safety screen: I read both chat messages, the driver's statement and the complaint; nothing constitutes a threat, intimidation, harassment, abuse or dangerous-driving allegation — "3 min up, cancelling the trip" is a routine cancellation notice, not an abuse [F9][F10][F12][SAFE-1]. The only money in dispute is the fee, with no surge applied, so the outcome is no_action and no amount is payable [F7][F8][NS-0].

rejected_claims.reason: Reading of NS-1 (iii) is wrong on the record: the post-tap period is 220 s continuously inside 200 m, above the 180 s threshold, so (iii) is satisfied rather than failed; the 17:22 chat message is a statement, not a clock, and does not shorten the measured wait [F6][F4][F10][NS-1].

The longer pre-tap presence does not make the post-tap wait incomplete: NS-1 (iii) counts from the tap [F6], and the driver's statement (F12) adds nothing because untimed/statement-based accounts cannot displace the system records [F5][F6][F12][NS-1].
NS-2 only applies when an NS-1 element fails; (i)(ii)(iii) are all met on the trace and records, so no full refund of the $6.61 arises [F6][F7][NS-1][NS-2].

NS-2's flag_account limb is confined to a tap made while outside the pickup radius, which did not occur here (41 m at the tap) [F6][NS-2]; RD-6 requires an established refundable breach, and profile facts (F17) cannot alone support the flag [F17][RD-6].

Not adopted as the basis for the wait: NS-1 (iii) runs from the 17:19:15 tap, so the 5 min 5 s inside 200 m from 17:17:50 (F2, F5) is not the measured period, though the post-tap 220 s independently satisfies the threshold [F2][F5][F6][NS-1].
The driver's 17:22 warning (F10) does not create the entitlement; the fee rests on the tap plus the measured continuous wait, not on notifying the rider [F10][F6][NS-1].
Correct that profile history cannot decide the case, but the driver's 2 upheld no-show disputes (F17) also do not create a flag on this trip, since no breach is established [F17][RD-6][NS-2].
